reasons.claim: The market cap of 7 billion is well below the 15 billion the business could be worth once the targeted 1.5 billion EBITDA is reached at a typical 10x multiple, implying a roughly 2x return.
reasons.quote: so 1 Point 5 billion ibita compared to the current market cap of 7 billion these companies often go for 10 times iita so the potential for this company is to be at 15 billion so that's a 2X from where we are plus the dividend

data_check.gap_note: not in our data: target EBITDA

reasons.claim: The 2023 collapse is a temporary destocking-driven headwind against a structurally positive long-term demand trend for crop protection, so the drop is a buying opportunity rather than a permanent impairment.
reasons.quote: this might be a situation when we have a temporary headwinds creating a long-term buying opportunity for us investors

reasons.claim: Falling EBITDA pushed leverage against debt covenants, a real risk though management secured an amendment to give room.
reasons.quote: we have financial leverage problem as their iita went down their covenants got broken but they have had a deal they have made an amendment to the credit agreement

data_check.gap_note: he says 6.5, as-of 3.274e+09 (FY2022); annual vs TTM or a different definition

reasons.claim: A well-covered, growing dividend plus buybacks make FMC an attractive income and capital-return story alongside the growth case.
reasons.quote: so if they can keep that 300 million for dividends that's a 4% so this is also an interesting dividend investment

data_check.gap_note: he says 300, as-of 2.1381 (FY2022); annual vs TTM or a different definition

reasons.claim: Despite the attractive setup he will not personally cover or invest in FMC because agrochemicals are outside what he enjoys following.
reasons.quote: herbicides insecticides is not really a thing I'm a fan of

external_facts_used: Company cut 2023 guidance while raising 2026 guidance
Investor day target of 1.5 billion EBITDA by 2024-2026 with high return on invested capital
Credit agreement amendment setting leverage covenants of 6.5x through June 2024 and 3.75x thereafter
1999/2019 spin-off of Livent, now worth about 3 billion in market cap
FMC named one of America's most responsible companies

critic.notes: ok — he calls it a good business at fair price with ~12% return and 'could be a good buy', but personally passes; watchlist/diversified-portfolio candidate fits fair_hold.
